threats.scenario: Scenario 3 — LLM-Integrated Account Recovery & Profile Management
threats.data_flow_ref: DF8: Recovery Token Submission / DF9: Forwarded Token Credential
threats.threat_description: Recovery token brute-forcing: Attacker submits automated token guesses via DF8/DF9 to hijack victim accounts during active recovery windows.
threats.attack_preconditions: Short, low-entropy, or unthrottled recovery tokens.
threats.architecture_evidence: P2 validates submitted recovery credentials (DF9) against DS2. Weak entropy or unthrottled verification allows brute-forcing.
threats.mitigation: Generate high-entropy tokens (>= 128 bits CSPRNG), enforce strict attempt throttling (e.g., 5 attempts max), and invalidate token upon repeated failures.
threats.cvss_rationale: Network vector, low complexity, no privileges required, High Confidentiality and Integrity impact.
threats.reviewer_validation_basis: Audited against architecture: P2 processes unauthenticated token verification submissions across Zone A -> Zone B.

threats.scenario: Scenario 3 — LLM-Integrated Account Recovery & Profile Management
threats.threat_description: Recovery token replay: P2 fails to atomically consume/invalidate recovery tokens in DS2 (DF12) upon first use, enabling an attacker to reuse intercepted tokens.
threats.attack_preconditions: Recovery token remains marked as active in DS2 after initial successful verification.
threats.security_impact: Unauthorized re-authentication and repeated account takeover.
threats.architecture_evidence: Workflow step 15 requires: 'A valid recovery token is consumed or invalidated so that it cannot be reused.' Flaws in invalidation logic permit replay.
threats.mitigation: Enforce atomic, single-use token consumption within the same database transaction that validates the recovery credential.
threats.cvss_rationale: Network vector, low complexity, no privileges required, High Confidentiality and Integrity impact.
threats.reviewer_validation_basis: Audited against architecture: Workflow step 15 mandates single-use token invalidation in DS2.

threats.scenario: Scenario 3 — LLM-Integrated Account Recovery & Profile Management
threats.data_flow_ref: DF1: Recovery Initiation Request / DF7: Recovery Challenge
threats.threat_description: Account recovery user enumeration: Differential response messages or timing on DF7 reveal whether an account exists in DS1.
threats.attack_preconditions: Attacker initiates recovery requests with varying target usernames/emails.
threats.security_impact: Discovery of valid user accounts for targeted phishing or brute-force attacks.
threats.architecture_evidence: P2 queries DS1 (DF3/DF4) and returns recovery challenges (DF7). Explicit requirement mandates addressing recovery-request enumeration.
threats.mitigation: Return uniform generic responses ('If the account exists, recovery instructions have been dispatched') with standardized execution timing.
threats.cvss_rationale: Network vector, low complexity, no privileges required, Low Confidentiality impact.
threats.reviewer_validation_basis: Audited against architecture: P2 generates external recovery challenge DF7 across Zone A -> Zone B.

threats.scenario: Scenario 3 — LLM-Integrated Account Recovery & Profile Management
threats.data_flow_ref: DF13: Authorized Profile Update Request / DF14: Profile Modification Query
threats.threat_description: Mass assignment / parameter tampering on profile update: Attacker submits unauthorized attributes (e.g. `role: admin`, `status: verified`) in profile update payload.
threats.attack_preconditions: Profile update request parsing accepts arbitrary object properties.
threats.security_impact: Privilege escalation and unauthorized modification of account security status.
threats.architecture_evidence: Workflow step 18 requires: 'The request must contain only the profile changes that the recovered/authorized user is permitted to make.'
threats.mitigation: Enforce strict schema whitelisting for permitted profile modification fields, rejecting any administrative or internal attributes.
threats.cvss_rationale: Network vector, low complexity, requires low privileges, High Confidentiality and Integrity impact.
threats.reviewer_validation_basis: Audited against architecture: P3 modifies user account records in DS1 upon receiving update requests.

threats.scenario: Scenario 3 — LLM-Integrated Account Recovery & Profile Management
threats.data_flow_ref: DF20: Support Prompt + Approved Context -> P5 / DF21: Outbound Prompt Request -> EE2
threats.threat_description: Leakage of recovery secrets to external LLM: P4/P5 includes raw recovery tokens, temporary passwords, or reset secrets in the prompt sent across Zone D.
threats.attack_preconditions: Improper context assembly logic in P4 passes raw authentication secrets into prompt builder.
threats.security_impact: Exposure of sensitive recovery credentials to third-party LLM provider.
threats.architecture_evidence: Explicit requirement mandates: 'The AI assistant must not receive raw recovery tokens, passwords, password-reset secrets, or unnecessary sensitive authentication material.'
threats.mitigation: Architecturally isolate P4 from recovery secret data and enforce automated regex-based secret redaction on all outgoing prompt payloads.
threats.cvss_rationale: Network vector, low complexity, requires low privileges, High Confidentiality impact.
threats.reviewer_validation_basis: Audited against architecture: Explicit constraint restricts transmission of reset secrets across Zone B -> Zone D.

threats.scenario: Scenario 3 — LLM-Integrated Account Recovery & Profile Management
threats.data_flow_ref: DF18: User Account Question / DF24: Generated AI Answer
threats.owasp_top_10_for_llm: LLM06: Excessive Agency / Insecure Output Handling
threats.threat_description: Excessive trust in LLM output: Attacker uses prompt injection to trick LLM into generating fake authorization instructions that downstream components treat as valid recovery decisions.
threats.attack_preconditions: Downstream application components rely on LLM text output to trigger account state modifications.
threats.security_impact: Unauthorized account recovery, token creation, or profile modification.
threats.architecture_evidence: Explicit constraint: 'The generated LLM response is untrusted output and must not directly trigger account recovery, profile modification, token creation, authorization, or authentication decisions.'
threats.mitigation: Ensure LLM responses are treated strictly as untrusted text, and never allow LLM output to directly invoke or authorize state-modifying operations.
threats.cvss_rationale: Network vector, low complexity, no privileges required, High Confidentiality and Integrity impact.
threats.reviewer_validation_basis: Audited against architecture: Explicit constraint forbids downstream components from trusting LLM text output.

threats.scenario: Scenario 3 — LLM-Integrated Account Recovery & Profile Management
threats.data_flow_ref: DF5: Store Recovery Token Request / DF10: Token Validation Query
threats.threat_description: Storage of plaintext recovery tokens in DS2: Unauthorized read access to token storage allows an attacker to compromise all active recovery tokens across the application.
threats.attack_preconditions: Direct read access or SQL/NoSQL injection on DS2 token storage.
threats.security_impact: Widespread account takeover via compromise of all active recovery tokens.
threats.architecture_evidence: DS2 stores active recovery tokens, expiration, and state. Requirement addresses token-storage compromise.
threats.mitigation: Store recovery tokens as salted cryptographic hashes (e.g. SHA-256) in DS2, verifying hashes in constant time during validation.
threats.cvss_rationale: Network vector, low complexity, requires high privileges, High Confidentiality impact.
threats.reviewer_validation_basis: Audited against architecture: DS2 holds token data accessed by P2 across Zone B -> Zone C.

threats.scenario: Scenario 3 — LLM-Integrated Account Recovery & Profile Management
threats.data_flow_ref: DF1: Recovery Initiation Request / DF2: Forwarded Recovery Request
threats.threat_description: High-volume automated recovery initiation requests exhaust notification provider quotas (SMS/Email) and server queues, denying recovery services to legitimate users.
threats.attack_preconditions: Attacker initiates large volumes of recovery requests targeting various accounts.
threats.security_impact: Exhaustion of notification capacity and denial of service for legitimate account recoveries.
threats.architecture_evidence: P2 processes recovery requests from Zone A. Requirement explicitly dictates protection against denial of service and resource exhaustion.
threats.mitigation: Implement per-IP and per-account rate limits, CAPTCHA on recovery initiation, and multi-tier notification provider fallbacks.
threats.cvss_rationale: Network vector, low complexity, no privileges required, High Availability impact.
threats.reviewer_validation_basis: Audited against architecture: P2 handles public recovery requests without pre-authentication.
